vision: A distributable library of AI coding assistant rules, skills, hooks, and an adversarial verification harness for Cursor and Claude Code. The library must dogfood its own authoring standards: every rule, skill, and validation gate should pass before the library is considered trustworthy.
direction: library/cursor/ is the single source of truth for distributable config. .cursor/ is local-only (gitignored, created via make setup). Validation (make validate) must pass with zero errors. The eval pipeline (Tier 1 static + Tier 3 session scenarios) measures whether agents actually follow the rules. Current focus: eval pipeline accuracy — reducing false negatives from SDK bridge limitations.

trade_offs.alternative: Keep symlinks tracked, gitignore only transient files
trade_offs.reasoning: Matches how consumer projects treat IDE config; library/cursor/ is the distributable artifact

trade_offs.alternative: Demote bulky rules to alwaysApply: false
trade_offs.reasoning: Keeps universal guidance available but risks agents not loading security/code standards on non-matching globs
Preserves one entry point (/adversarial-harness) while meeting line limits
spec.md was read once (plan gate) then became stale. Single file eliminates drift by design.

trade_offs.alternative: Full protocol checks on all scenarios
trade_offs.reasoning: Behavioral/pushback scenarios should only test behavioral traits, not harness protocol compliance

open_questions: Should the eval pipeline inject harness protocol instructions into the agent's system prompt for SDK sessions (simulating hooks/skills)?
How to handle gap-2/gap-4: is it a harness skill guidance issue or a fundamental SDK bridge limitation?

features.name: Documentation drifts silently when code changes — no automated staleness detection
features.details: Docs (README, EVAL_GUIDE, SKILL.md, HARNESS_STANDARD) went stale after spec.md kill, harness rule trim, and long scenarios addition. No lint or hook detects when a code change invalidates doc references. Potential fixes: (1) a doc-coherence lint that cross-checks Makefile targets, state files, and doc references, (2) a stop hook that flags multi-file changes touching code but not docs, (3) a periodic audit scenario in the eval pipeline.
